_readme: The ONE place that says which Supabase project each environment belongs to.
Why this file exists: the backup workflow was called 'Backup Production Database' and backed
up QA. Nothing detected that, because 'production' was a word in a filename rather than a
value anyone checked. Every consumer now reads this file: the app's environment guard
(src/lib/environmentContract.ts), the build gate (vite.config.ts), the audit script, and the
backup/restore tooling. Changing a project ref here changes it everywhere, and the checks that
compare a live connection against these refs will fail closed if the two disagree.
A project ref is NOT a secret: it is already in the repository, in .env.qa, and in every
Supabase URL the app builds. It is here so that tooling can refuse to operate on the wrong
project. Credentials are never stored here.
environmentRefs are also the credentials prefix each environment must use, so a production
backup cannot be run with staging secrets by accident: see scripts/lib/environments.mjs.
clusterId is the Postgres cluster fingerprint (pg_control_system().system_identifier). It is
needed because Supabase's pooler rewrites current_user to 'postgres', so the server cannot be
asked which project it is (measured 2026-10-01: current_user = 'postgres', and
current_setting('supabase.project_ref') = NULL). The fingerprint is recorded here on the first
verified run and compared on every later one, so a cluster swap is detected rather than assumed
away.
localEnvFile names the gitignored file a local run may read credentials from. It is null for
development and production on purpose: there is no development project, and production's
credentials must come from repository secrets or an explicit export so that none of them can
end up in the checkout.

development.notes: No development project exists yet. .env.local points at the staging project. Because there is no ref to verify against, the backup tooling refuses to run for this environment rather than guess.

staging.notes: Named 'Agri-shop-App-QA' in the dashboard and called QA throughout this repository. It is the staging target: the E2E lane, the QA scripts and both local env files use it. It also holds the engineering tooling's own tables (incident_*, impact_*, engineering_memory).

production.notes: Named 'Agrishop APp'. Confirmed as production on 2026-10-01 and confirmed to hold real business data (1 shop, 4 users, 6 customers, 52 sales). Runs on the Free plan, which provides no managed backups, no downloadable backups and no PITR.
